vibe: Patch the exposed edge first: Pixel, ScreenConnect, WordPress and hosting tools are under active attack, while AWS offers a sobering lesson in cross-region resilience.

cyber.title: Google fixes actively exploited Pixel modem zero-day
cyber.summary: Google patched CVE-2026-81224, a Pixel modem information-disclosure flaw used in limited targeted attacks. Pixel owners should install the September update now; enterprise fleets should verify patch compliance.

cyber.title: Critical ScreenConnect flaw is now actively exploited
cyber.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-20079 to its exploited-vulnerabilities catalogue. Patch internet-facing ConnectWise ScreenConnect servers immediately and review them for compromise.

cyber.title: WooCommerce plugin flaw exploited to plant PHP web shells
cyber.summary: Attackers are exploiting an unauthenticated file-upload bug in the Wholesale Lead Capture plugin. Update or remove the plugin and inspect affected WordPress hosts for web shells.

cyber.title: Acronis cPanel backup plugin flaw exploited in targeted attacks
cyber.summary: Acronis says attackers are exploiting a cPanel backup-plugin vulnerability. Hosting operators should update promptly and hunt for suspicious plugin or account activity.

cyber.title: Malware bypasses browser checks to force-install extensions
cyber.summary: New malware manipulates Chrome and Edge policy controls to install unwanted extensions, a useful reminder to monitor enterprise browser-policy changes as closely as endpoint binaries.

cyber.title: BragJack turns browser agents against their users
cyber.summary: Researchers describe prompt-injection techniques that can steer browser-based AI agents through hostile page content. Keep high-privilege agent actions gated by explicit confirmation.

cyber.title: One malicious extension can hijack multiple browser AI assistants
cyber.summary: A cross-browser extension attack shows how shared extension trust can expose Chrome, Edge, Comet, Opera Neon and Claude workflows. Audit extensions before granting agent access to sensitive sessions.

cyber.title: Issabel command-execution flaw under active attack
cyber.summary: Attackers are exploiting an unauthenticated OS-command-injection flaw in Issabel deployments. Exposed communications servers should be patched or isolated quickly.

cyber.title: Hackers publish driver data after Florida motor-vehicle breach
cyber.summary: Thousands of driver records were published following a breach of a Florida motor-vehicle database, extending the identity-fraud risk from the wider licence-data campaign.

ai.title: OpenAI expands ChatGPT advertising with sponsored agents
ai.summary: OpenAI is extending ads beyond static placements into sponsored conversational agents. It is a significant shift in ChatGPT's business model and raises fresh questions about disclosure and answer neutrality.

ai.title: Anthropic merges Claude and Cowork, adds editable documents
ai.summary: Claude can now produce and revise editable documents and presentations inside one interface, collapsing the boundary between chat and workspace tooling.

ai.title: Google releases Gemini 3.8 Live models for production voice agents
ai.summary: Google's new Live and Extended Thinking variants target lower-latency, production-grade voice agents. The longer-reasoning option is the technically interesting part for complex spoken workflows.

ai.title: Google opens Home devices to third-party AI agents via MCP
ai.summary: Google is adding an MCP integration that lets outside agents control compatible smart-home devices. Useful, but permission boundaries and confirmation flows will matter enormously.

ai.title: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google coordinate on AI safety
ai.summary: The three leading labs have held weeks of talks on shared safety work, while OpenAI backs independent model assessments. Rare cross-lab coordination makes this worth watching.

it.title: AWS says wartime damage permanently destroyed some cloud resources
it.summary: AWS says physical damage in the Middle East left some customer resources unrecoverable. It is a stark reminder that availability zones are not a substitute for tested cross-region backups and recovery.

it.title: Salesforce recovers from a global outage
it.summary: Salesforce restored service after a broad outage disrupted customers worldwide. Cloud teams should review dependency maps and degraded-mode plans for core SaaS platforms.

it.title: Rheinmetall open-sources its Battlesuite connected-system protocol
it.summary: The defence manufacturer published documentation for its onboard connected-system API. It is niche, but an unusual look at interoperability in military platforms.

videos.title: DOP 368: The AI Productivity Paradox
videos.verdict: SKIM — strong thesis, but the podcast is long; the opening framing and DORA discussion carry the value
videos.summary: AI coding tools make individuals feel faster, yet teams may ship no more customer value and can create more instability. The useful takeaway is to measure flow, quality and outcomes—not tickets closed or code produced.

videos.title: The vulnpocalypse might not be so bad after all
videos.verdict: SKIM — practical security discussion; focus on validation, identity and managed degradation
videos.summary: IBM's panel argues the AI-driven 'vulnpocalypse' is overstated: validate whether a CVE is exploitable in your environment, keep identity fundamentals strong, and plan which critical services survive a prolonged incident.

videos.title: GNOME 51: a look at everything that changed
videos.verdict: SKIM — worthwhile for Linux desktop users; use the chaptered feature tour
videos.summary: GNOME 51 brings better reduced-motion behaviour, crisper SVG cursors, improved hybrid-GPU frame handling, broader login methods and many application refinements rather than one headline feature.

videos.title: New Way Now: Wipro scales agentic AI for 15,000 associates with Google Cloud Consulting
videos.verdict: SKIM — polished customer case study, light on implementation detail
videos.summary: Wipro says it deployed Gemini Enterprise to 15,000 staff and orchestrates roughly 90 agents with Google Cloud. The clearest lesson is that process orchestration matters more than merely buying agent tooling.

videos.title: AI Says It's a 10/10 Vulnerability... But Is It? 🤔
videos.verdict: SKIM — only a short clip, but the advice is sound
videos.summary: Do not accept an AI-generated CVSS-style severity at face value: first test whether the issue applies to your environment and business, then verify the model's judgement.
